name: aer_inject
prose: Injects a fake AER error (aer_inject.c:319-484; the slice cut the head). It looks up the PCI device from einj->domain/bus/dev/fn and returns -ENODEV at once if it is not found (nothing was acquired yet). From then on every path ends at out_put, which kfrees the two scratch records (a record is NULL if it was handed over to the einjected list, so the kfree is then a no-op) and drops the device reference with pci_dev_put. It finds the root port (or the device's RCEC): -ENODEV if neither exists; -EPROTONOSUPPORT if the device or the root port has no AER capability; -ENOMEM if either kzalloc fails. If aer_mask_override is set it temporarily writes the correctable and uncorrectable mask registers (each mask is ANDed with a logical not of the injected status, so it becomes 0 when that status is non-zero and is cut to its bit 0 otherwise) and restores the original values after the locked update. Under inject_lock it creates (taking err_alloc, adding to the einjected list) or reuses the device's error record and ORs in the injected status and header log. If aer_mask_override is clear and a non-zero injected correctable or uncorrectable status is entirely masked by the device it unlocks and returns -EINVAL (the device record is already updated, the root port record is not, and no bus ops are installed). Otherwise it creates or reuses the root port's record and sets its root status and source id, installs the AER config ops on the device's bus and then on the root port's bus (a pci_bus_set_aer_ops error is returned; the second call only after the first succeeded), then finds the AER service device of the root port: -ENODEV if there is none, -EPROTONOSUPPORT if its service data is not initialised, else it returns irq_inject_interrupt(edev->irq).

name: pcie_do_recovery
prose: Runs PCIe error recovery for dev and returns the resulting pci_ers_result_t (err.c:210-299; the slice shows only the tail, starting after the slot_reset step; the name 'unnamed_recovery_fn' is not in the source). In the tail: if status is not PCI_ERS_RESULT_RECOVERED it jumps to the failed label. Otherwise it broadcasts the resume callback with pci_walk_bridge(bridge, report_resume, &status); if the host bridge has native AER control (or pcie_ports_native) it clears the device status and the non-fatal AER status of dev; it then walks the bridge with pci_pm_runtime_put, logs 'device recovery successful' and returns status. The failed path (also reached earlier when reset_subordinates(bridge) does not return PCI_ERS_RESULT_RECOVERED) does pci_pm_runtime_put on the bridge, reports a permanent failure with report_perm_failure_detected, logs 'device recovery failed' and returns status as it then stands: normally not RECOVERED, but a failed subordinate reset can leave an earlier RECOVERED value in status.

name: __pci_read_base
prose: Sizes one BAR or the ROM BAR of dev and fills res (probe.c:219-341; the slice cut the head). type is pci_bar_unknown for an ordinary BAR (flags come from decode_bar, plus IORESOURCE_SIZEALIGN) or the ROM type (IORESOURCE_ROM_ENABLE if the enable bit is set in the register). It sets res->name to the device name, reads the BAR at pos and takes the pre-read sizing word sizes[0] (for a 64-bit memory BAR also the upper dword and sizes[1]); all-ones values count as 0. If the size mask is 0, or pci_size() cannot size it, it takes the fail path: res->flags becomes 0 (the start/end are not touched). A 64-bit BAR with a size over 4 GB on a build where pci_bus_addr_t or resource_size_t is narrower than 64 bits is flagged IORESOURCE_UNSET|IORESOURCE_DISABLED with range 0..0 and an error is logged; a 64-bit BAR whose upper dword (re-read into l at pos + 4) is non-zero when pci_bus_addr_t is narrower than 64 bits is flagged IORESOURCE_UNSET with range 0..size-1; both keep IORESOURCE_MEM_64 and skip the conversion. Otherwise it converts the bus region to a resource with pcibios_bus_to_resource and, if converting back does not give the original start, marks it IORESOURCE_UNSET with start 0 and end = size-1. The return value is 1 if res->flags still has IORESOURCE_MEM_64 and 0 otherwise, so the fail path returns 0 but the two above-4GB paths and a normal 64-bit BAR return 1. It logs the resource when res->flags is non-zero.

name: pci_scan_bridge_extend
prose: Scans (pass 0) or assigns bus numbers to (pass 1) the secondary bus of the bridge dev on bus and returns the highest subordinate bus number used, as the new max (probe.c:1355-1581; the slice cut the head). It calls pm_runtime_get_sync(dev) first, reads the bus numbers and ignores a hard-wired primary 0, and marks the bridge broken in pass 0 if its configuration is not sensible; it disables Master-Abort mode in PCI_BRIDGE_CONTROL (bctl saved). Every path ends at out, which clears the Secondary Status register, restores PCI_BRIDGE_CONTROL to bctl, calls pm_runtime_put and returns max (the PCI_STATUS clear is only done in the pass-1 assignment branch, not at out). Firmware-configured case (a secondary or subordinate number set, not pcibios_assign_all_busses, not CardBus, not broken): in pass 1 it goes to out with max unchanged; in pass 0 it finds or creates (pci_add_new_bus, goto out on failure) the child bus for the existing secondary number, scans it with pci_scan_child_bus_extend, warns if its max exceeds subordinate, and sets max to subordinate if that is larger. It does not reprogram the bridge's numbers. Assignment case: in pass 0 it goes to out with max unchanged (first writing the primary/secondary/subordinate register to zero in the low 24 bits if pcibios_assign_all_busses, broken or CardBus); in pass 1 it clears PCI_STATUS, takes the EA fixed secondary number if present else max+1, finds or creates the child (goto out with max unchanged if creating fails), does max++ and decrements available_buses if non-zero, writes the three bus numbers in a single dword write (CardBus latency timer too), scans the child with pci_scan_child_bus_extend(child, available_buses) (max = its result) or, for CardBus, adds up to CARDBUS_RESERVE_BUSNR numbers to max, uses the EA fixed subordinate as max if present, updates the child's busn_res end and writes PCI_SUBORDINATE_BUS with max. In both cases that reach a child it names the child bus and logs a message if the child's bus range does not fit inside its ancestors; those paths return max (the maximum or the child-scan result).

name: calculate_iosize
prose: Computes the I/O window size for a bridge (setup-bus.c:1039-1062). Starting from size it raises it to min_size if smaller, treats old_size == 1 as 0, and, if CONFIG_ISA or CONFIG_EISA is set, applies the ISA aliasing transform size = (size & 0xff) + ((size & ~0xffUL) << 2). It then adds size1, takes the larger of that and add_size, adds children_add_size, and returns ALIGN(max(that, old_size), align). It has no side effects. In arithmetic on resource_size_t the sums may wrap if the arguments are huge; ALIGN assumes align is a power of two.

name: vga_arb_write
prose: Write handler of the VGA arbiter device file (vgaarb.c:1125-1371; the slice cut the head). It returns -EINVAL if count >= 64, -EFAULT if copy_from_user fails, then NUL-terminates the copy and dispatches on its prefix; a message that matches none of 'lock ', 'unlock ', 'trylock ', 'target ' and 'decodes ' returns -EPROTO. 'lock': -EPROTO if the iostate does not parse or is VGA_RSRC_NONE, -ENODEV if no target is set, else vga_get_uninterruptible() (blocking until acquired) and, if the target has a card slot, io_cnt/mem_cnt incremented for the requested legacy resources; returns count. 'unlock': the argument 'all' means legacy IO and MEM, otherwise the iostate must parse (-EPROTO; VGA_RSRC_NONE is accepted); -ENODEV if no target; -EINVAL if the target has no card slot in priv->cards, or a requested legacy IO or MEM resource has a zero count; else vga_put() and the counts are decremented; returns count. 'trylock': -EPROTO (bad iostate), -ENODEV (no target), -EBUSY if vga_tryget() fails, else the counts are incremented and count is returned. 'target': 'default' takes a reference on vga_default_device() (may be NULL), otherwise the PCI address must parse (-EPROTO) and the device exist (-ENODEV); if the device is not a known VGA device (vgadev_find fails, which includes a NULL pdev) it drops the reference if any and returns -ENODEV; otherwise priv->target is set to it and a free (or matching) card slot is registered with zeroed counts; if all MAX_USER_CARDS slots are taken it releases the reference and returns -ENOMEM, with priv->target already set; on success it releases the reference and returns count (priv->target keeps the pointer without holding the reference). 'decodes': -EPROTO for a bad iostate, -ENODEV with no target, else __vga_set_legacy_decoding(target, iostate, true) and count.

name: meson_ddr_pmu_create
prose: Creates and registers the Amlogic DDR bandwidth PMU for a platform device (meson_ddr_pmu_core.c:482-553; the name meson_ddr_pmu_probe is not in the source, the slice cut the head). It allocates the ddr_pmu with devm_kzalloc (-ENOMEM on failure), initialises the perf pmu callbacks, parses the device tree (error returned if ddr_pmu_parse_dt < 0), fills the format attributes, records the current CPU, and builds the name with devm_kasprintf (-ENOMEM if it fails). It sets up a dynamic multi-instance cpuhp state (a negative return is returned at once; otherwise the value is stored in pmu->cpuhp_state), adds the instance without callbacks (on error it removes the cpuhp state and returns that error), fills the event attributes and registers the PMU with perf_pmu_register(-1) (on error it removes the instance and the cpuhp state and returns that error). On success it stores name, dev, pmu_enabled = false, sets the platform drvdata and returns 0. On failure drvdata is not set and the PMU is not registered.

name: arm_cspmu_get_name
prose: Builds a device-managed name for an Arm CoreSight PMU (arm_cspmu.c:248-285; the slice cut the head). It looks up the ACPI APMT node of cspmu->dev. With no node it returns devm_kasprintf of PMUNAME "_%u" with an atomic_fetch_inc of the type-0 counter pmu_idx[0]. With a node, if its type is >= ACPI_APMT_NODE_TYPE_COUNT it logs an error and returns NULL. For an ACPI-type node it copies the 8-byte primary instance to a zeroed string and returns devm_kasprintf of "%s_%s_%s_%u" with PMUNAME, the type string, that HID string and inst_secondary (no counter is incremented in this branch); for any other type it returns devm_kasprintf of "%s_%s_%d" with PMUNAME, the type string and atomic_fetch_inc of that type's counter. A NULL result from devm_kasprintf is passed through (so NULL is also returned on allocation failure). The returned string belongs to the device (freed with it).

name: arm_acpi_register_pmu_device
prose: Registers an Arm PMU platform device after checking that the GICC entries of all possible CPUs agree (arm_pmu_acpi.c:72-126; static, __maybe_unused). It returns -ENXIO if pdev->num_resources != 1 or if resource[0].flags is not exactly IORESOURCE_IRQ. For each possible CPU it fetches the MADT GICC entry; if its header length is shorter than len it returns -ENXIO when a non-zero GSI has already been recorded and 0 otherwise (nothing registered). It parses the GSI and the heterogeneity id; while no non-zero GSI has been recorded the first CPU's values are stored (a zero GSI is overwritten by the next CPU's values), afterwards any CPU whose hetero id or GSI differs (including a zero GSI after a non-zero one) makes it warn and return -ENXIO. After the loop, if the last parsed GSI is zero (so also if all were zero or there is no possible CPU) it returns 0 without registering. Otherwise it calls acpi_register_gsi (a negative result gives a warning and -ENXIO), stores the IRQ in resource[0].start and returns platform_device_register(pdev); if that fails (non-zero) it calls acpi_unregister_gsi(gsi) before returning its error (resource[0].start is left set).

name: arm_spe_pmu_start
prose: Starts SPE (Statistical Profiling Extension) sampling for event on this CPU (arm_spe_pmu.c:851-889; the slice cut the head). It sets hwc->state = 0 first, then calls arm_spe_perf_aux_output_begin(handle, event); if that returns non-zero it calls arm_spe_pmu_stop(event, 0) and returns (stop, with the state now cleared, does not return early: it writes PMSCR_EL1 = 0 and PMBLIMITR_EL1 = 0 to disable and drain, and sets PERF_HES_STOPPED; no filter or interval registers are programmed by start). Otherwise it writes PMSFCR_EL1, PMSEVFR_EL1, PMSNEVFR_EL1 (only when SPE_PMU_FEAT_INV_FILT_EVT is set) and PMSLATFR_EL1 from the event configuration. Only if flags includes PERF_EF_RELOAD it writes PMSIRR_EL1 from the event config (arm_spe_event_to_pmsirr), issues an isb, then writes PMSICR_EL1 from hwc->period_left. Finally it computes PMSCR from the event, issues an isb and writes PMSCR_EL1, enabling sampling. It returns nothing.

name: sun4i_usb_phy_probe
prose: Platform probe of the Allwinner sun4i USB PHY driver (phy-sun4i-usb.c:719-904; the slice cut the head). It allocates the driver data with devm_kzalloc (-ENOMEM), initialises the lock and the detect delayed work, sets drvdata, and gets the match data (-EINVAL if none). It maps the 'phy_ctrl' resource, gets the optional id-detect and vbus-detect GPIOs and, only if the device-tree property usb0_vbus_power-supply is present, looks up that power supply; each of these steps returns the error code of the failing devm call, and an absent supply (the getter returns NULL) returns -EPROBE_DEFER. It reads the dr_mode, allocates and registers the extcon device (errors returned). Then for each index i below MAX_PHYS not in cfg->missing_phys it gets the reset control (-ENOENT ends the loop at that index, any other error is returned), the optional vbus regulator (-EPROBE_DEFER is returned; any other error sets phy->vbus to NULL), the PHY clock, a secondary clock (the HSIC clock is required for the HSIC index, otherwise pmu%d_clk is optional), the pmu register mapping for i > 0 or cfg->phy0_dual_route, and creates the PHY (errors returned). It then sets num_phys to the loop index reached. The id-detect IRQ is requested when gpiod_to_irq gives a positive number (error returned without calling sun4i_usb_phy_remove); the vbus-detect IRQ likewise, but on failure it sets vbus_det_irq to -1, calls sun4i_usb_phy_remove and returns the error. If a vbus power supply exists it registers the notifier (on failure it calls sun4i_usb_phy_remove and returns the error) and sets vbus_power_nb_registered. Finally it registers the PHY provider (on failure sun4i_usb_phy_remove and the error) and returns 0. All devm resources are released by devres on any failure.

name: cdns_dphy_rx_get_band_ctrl
prose: Returns the index of the Cadence D-PHY RX band for a CSI-2 clock (cdns-dphy-rx.c:102-118). It computes rate = (hs_clk_rate / 1000000) * 2 as an unsigned int (Mbps, DDR); the doubling would wrap if hs_clk_rate / 1000000 reached 2^31. If rate is below bands[0].min_rate (80) it returns -EOPNOTSUPP (-95). Otherwise it returns the index i of the first of the 23 bands for which rate < bands[i].max_rate; the bands are contiguous ([80,100), [100,120), ... [2250,2500)), so the result is the band with min_rate <= rate < max_rate, 0 to 22. If rate is 2500 or more no band matches and it returns -EOPNOTSUPP. It has no side effects.

name: hi3670_pcie_phy_power_on
prose: Power-on callback of the HiSilicon Kirin 970 PCIe PHY (phy-hi3670-pcie.c:665-718; the slice cut the head). It writes the host power-supply bit in the sysctrl register, enables the OE, then calls kirin_pcie_clk_ctrl(phy, true): if that fails (clk_set_rate, or enabling any of the five kirin clocks, after which the function disables those already enabled) it returns the error immediately. It then writes the ISO, PCIe-assert and HPCLK registers, runs hi3670_pcie_natural_cfg and calls hi3670_pcie_allclk_ctrl(phy, true); on error it goes to disable_clks. It then clears the test-powerdown bit, deasserts the controller perst_n through the APB regmap and waits 10 us. If is_pipe_clk_stable() returns false it also goes to disable_clks with ret == 0, so the function returns 0 although the PIPE clock is not stable and the clocks have been turned off. Otherwise it runs hi3670_pcie_set_eyeparam and hi3670_pcie_noc_power(phy, false); on error it goes to disable_clks; else it returns 0. disable_clks calls kirin_pcie_clk_ctrl(phy, false) (turning off only the five kirin clocks; nothing else done earlier is undone) and returns ret. allclk_ctrl itself returns -EINVAL if the PLL cannot be enabled (nothing undone in it) or the clk_set_rate error, after switching off its gates and the PLL; noc_power returns -EINVAL if the NoC power status does not change.

name: cv1800_usb_phy_set_mode
prose: phy set_mode callback of the Sophgo CV1800 USB2 PHY (phy-cv1800-usb2.c:43-78). It logs the mode, then selects a value for the ID-override bits. For PHY_MODE_USB_DEVICE it clears PHY_VBUS_POWER in REG_USB_PHY_CTRL with regmap_clear_bits (the result is ignored) and uses PHY_ID_OVERWRITE_EN | PHY_ID_OVERWRITE_MODE_DEVICE (bits 6 and 7). For PHY_MODE_USB_HOST it sets PHY_VBUS_POWER with regmap_set_bits (result ignored) and uses PHY_ID_OVERWRITE_EN with the mode bit 0. For PHY_MODE_USB_OTG it returns 0 without touching hardware if the phy does not support OTG, otherwise reads REG_USB_PHY_CTRL (returning the error on failure) and uses FIELD_GET of the mode bit, which is 0 or 1 and so lies outside the update mask. Any other mode returns -EINVAL without touching hardware. The three supported cases end with return regmap_update_bits(REG_USB_PHY_CTRL, mask = ID_OVERWRITE_EN | ID_OVERWRITE_MODE, regval), which returns 0 or a negative errno. In the OTG case the value masked into bits 6-7 is always 0, so both the override-enable and the override-mode bits are cleared (the ID pin is no longer overridden), whatever was read.

name: tegra210_pex_uphy_enable
prose: Enables the Tegra210 PCIe UPHY PLL and lanes (xusb-tegra210.c:464-680; the slice cut the head). It returns 0 at once if pcie->enable is already set. Otherwise it calls clk_prepare_enable(pcie->pll) and returns its error (clock not enabled) if that fails. This happens before the PLLE hardware-sequence test, so pcie->pll is enabled on both paths that follow. If tegra210_plle_hw_sequence_is_enabled() is true it skips the PLL initialisation. Otherwise it deasserts pcie->rst (on failure it goes to disable: pll disabled and unprepared, error returned), programs the UPHY PLL registers and runs five polling loops of up to 100 ms each (CAL_DONE set, CAL_DONE clear, LOCKDET status, RCAL_DONE set, RCAL_DONE clear); if any loop times out it sets err = -ETIMEDOUT and goes to reset (pcie->rst asserted, then pll disabled and unprepared) and returns -ETIMEDOUT. After the loops it enables PLL hardware control, drops the override bits and starts the PLLE hardware sequence. Both paths then set pcie->enable = true, clear the PCIe-IDDQ-disable bit in XUSB_PADCTL_USB3_PAD_MUX for every lane (it sets the IDDQ_DISABLE bit per lane via |=) and return 0, leaving pcie->pll enabled and, in the full-init path, pcie->rst deasserted.

prose: Builds the pin tables of the MediaTek/Ralink MIPS pin controller (pinctrl-mtmips.c:248-314; static, the slice cut the head). It sets all gpio bytes to 1, clears the byte of every pin used by a function, sets pin 0 back to 1, and for each pin i devm-allocates a 5-byte name (-ENOMEM at once on failure, leaving the earlier pads filled) formatted as 'io%d' and stores number and name in pads[i]. name: msm_pinmux_set_mux
prose: pinmux set_mux callback of the Qualcomm MSM pin controller (pinctrl-msm.c:154-247; the arguments are (pctldev, function, group)). It looks up the group's msm_pingroup, builds the mux-field mask from mux_bit and nfuncs, and searches g->funcs for the function; the position found is i, the mux selector. If it is not found (i == nfuncs) it does WARN_ON and returns -EINVAL with nothing written. If an irq is mapped on the pin (d non-NULL), i != gpio_func and the pin's bit in pctrl->disabled_for_mux was not yet set, it sets the bit and calls disable_irq_nosync (this happens before the lock is taken). Under pctrl->lock (raw spinlock, irqsave) it reads the ctl register; if i == gpio_func, the output-enable bit is set and ever_gpio was not yet set for the group, it reads the io register and rewrites its out bit to equal the in bit (only if they differ), to avoid a glitch. Then, if soc->egpio_func is non-zero and i equals egpio_func (the comparison is with the selector index, not the function id), only the egpio_enable bit is cleared and only if the egpio_present bit is set, leaving the mux field unchanged; otherwise it replaces the mux field with i and, if egpio_func is non-zero and the egpio_present bit is set, sets egpio_enable. In both cases the ctl register is written back, and the lock is released. Afterwards, if an irq is mapped, i == gpio_func and the disabled_for_mux bit was set (it is cleared), it clears pending interrupt state (through irq_chip_set_parent_state when d has parent data and the pin is in skip_wake_irqs, otherwise with msm_ack_intr_status) and calls enable_irq. It then returns 0.

name: rzg2l_pinctrl_pinconf_get
prose: pin_config_get callback of the Renesas RZ/G2L pin controller (pinctrl-rzg2l.c:1262-1418; the slice cut the head). It returns -EINVAL if the pin has no drv_data. For a pin that is not a single-pin one it also returns -EINVAL if rzg2l_validate_pin fails. It then switches on the config parameter, always returning -EINVAL where noted and leaving *config unmodified on any error: INPUT_ENABLE needs the IEN capability and a non-zero IEN bit (arg = that bit); OUTPUT_ENABLE needs the OEN capability, arg = rzg2l_read_oen (its negative error is returned); POWER_SOURCE gives arg = rzg2l_get_power_source (negative error returned, no capability test); SLEW_RATE needs SR, arg = the raw bit; BIAS_DISABLE / PULL_UP / PULL_DOWN need PUPD, the register value is converted with hw_to_bias_param (negative error returned) and must equal the queried parameter (else -EINVAL), and arg is then 1 for all three, including BIAS_DISABLE; DRIVE_STRENGTH needs IOLH_A and no drive_strength_ua in the hardware config, and arg is the 3V3 group-A table value in mA; DRIVE_STRENGTH_UA needs one of IOLH_A/B/C and drive_strength_ua, takes the power source (negative error returned) and returns the microamp value; OUTPUT_IMPEDANCE_OHMS needs IOLH_B and a valid groupb table, arg = the table value at the register index; OPEN_DRAIN / PUSH_PULL need NOD and the read bit must match the queried parameter (else -EINVAL); INPUT_SCHMITT_ENABLE needs SMT and a non-zero bit; the RZ/V2H output-impedance parameter needs IOLH_RZV2H, arg = raw register value; any other parameter returns -ENOTSUPP. On success it stores pinconf_to_config_packed(param, arg) in *config and returns 0.

name: samsung_pinctrl_probe
prose: Platform probe of the Samsung pinctrl driver (pinctrl-samsung.c:1261-1331; the slice cut the head). It devm-allocates the driver data (-ENOMEM) and calls samsung_pinctrl_get_soc_data, returning its error (PTR_ERR) directly if it fails. From then on failures go through err_put_banks (samsung_banks_node_put, then return ret) or err_unregister (samsung_pinctrl_unregister first, then err_put_banks). It sets drvdata->dev, reads the optional irq (a negative value other than -ENXIO fails; a positive value is stored in drvdata->irq), runs the SoC's retention init if there is retention data (error pointer converted and returned), gets the optional prepared 'pclk' clock (error returned) and calls samsung_pinctrl_register (error returned, without unregistering). It then runs the optional eint_gpio_init and eint_wkup_init hooks and the pud-value init (the SoC's own or the generic one). samsung_gpiolib_register and pinctrl_enable failures go through err_unregister. On success it stores drvdata with platform_set_drvdata and returns 0 (the bank nodes are not released on success).

name: ssh_ptl_submit
prose: Submits a packet to the Surface Aggregator packet transport layer for transmission (ssh_packet_layer.c:1312-1349; not for re-submission, though p->ptl may already have been set by an upper layer's request submission). It returns -EINVAL if the packet fields are invalid: a flush packet that carries data or is marked sequenced, or a non-flush packet without data. If p->ptl is NULL it sets it to ptl (and it stays set even if the queueing then fails); if it is already set to a different transport layer it triggers WARN_ON and returns -EALREADY. It then pushes the packet onto the queue under the queue lock; the push checks in order: -ESHUTDOWN if the layer is shutting down, -EINVAL if the packet is locked (for example canceled before submission), -EALREADY if it is already queued, otherwise it takes a reference and adds it to the queue (priority ordered); a non-zero status is returned. After success, if the packet is not a blocking one or the pending count is below SSH_PTL_MAX_PENDING it wakes the tx thread, and it returns 0.

name: ssh_rtl_cancel_nonpending
prose: Cancels a request that is not pending at the packet layer, returning true if it was removed or completed here and false otherwise (ssh_request_layer.c:581-655; static). It reads the request's type flags and does a cmpxchg of r->state from just those flags to the enumerator SSH_REQUEST_SF_LOCKED_BIT (which, as written, is the plain value 0 and not BIT(...), so the cmpxchg actually sets the state to 0). If the cmpxchg succeeded (the state held only the type flags, i.e. unsubmitted) and r->packet.ptl is NULL, it marks the request completed and calls ssh_rtl_complete_with_status(r, -ECANCELED) (or just returns true if the completed bit was already set) and returns true. Otherwise it locks the queue and tests-and-clears the QUEUED bit: if the request was not queued it returns false (this covers requests already pending or transmitting, requests already completed or canceled so that the cmpxchg failed, and a successful cmpxchg with ptl set but nothing queued; the request is not completed then). If it was queued it sets the LOCKED bit, removes it from the queue list, drops the queue's reference with ssh_request_put, completes it with -ECANCELED unless COMPLETED was already set, and returns true.

name: ATTRIBUTE_PROPERTY_STORE(curr_val, type)
prose: Macro template (bioscfg.h:320-350) that generates a static sysfs store function curr_val##_store(kobj, attr, buf, count) for the HP BIOS configuration driver. It duplicates buf with kstrdup and returns -ENOMEM at once if that fails (in that case the credentials are not cleared). Otherwise it calls hp_enforce_single_line_input(attr_value, count); if that returns 0 it finds the instance with get_<type>_instance_id(kobj) and, if the index is non-negative, runs validate_<type>_input(i, attr_value). If the status is still 0 it calls hp_set_attribute(kobj->name, attr_value), and if that also succeeded it calls update_<type>_value(i, attr_value) and, if the instance requires physical presence, hp_set_reboot_and_signal_event(). Note that when no instance matches (index -EIO) the status stays 0, so hp_set_attribute and the update/index use still run with the negative index; there is no -EIO return in that case. Finally it calls hp_clear_all_credentials(), frees the duplicate and returns the error status if non-zero, otherwise count.
